title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a decision that sets out its authority and framework for managing artificial intelligence initiatives. The decision outlines roles, responsibilities, and procedures for evaluating, approving, and overseeing AI projects to ensure responsible and compliant use.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy explains how the organization is hiring technology specialists to work in an AI office. It details the roles, qualifications, and responsibilities for these specialists, and sets guidelines for their work and compliance.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: An announcement for an open position for the Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office, outlining the main responsibilities such as overseeing scientific research, guiding policy, and ensuring ethical AI deployment. It also provides details on required qualifications, application procedures, and expected collaboration with other teams.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy explains how the AI Office will fill empty Legal Officer positions, detailing the qualifications, duties, and steps for selecting and appointing new hires. It also clarifies the role’s responsibilities in ensuring the office complies with AI regulations and supports its legal and strategic needs.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy document explains how to fill open positions for AI policy officers, outlining the required qualifications and responsibilities. It also sets guidelines for their work to ensure AI initiatives are aligned with legal, ethical, and organizational standards.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with reviewing the technical and societal impacts of AI systems under the proposed EU AI Act. They provide evidence‑based recommendations to help shape regulations that ensure safety, fairness, and transparency in AI deployment.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This document presents a draft request for establishing standard guidelines and procedures. It seeks to promote consistency, accountability, and safety in the development and use of AI systems.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces the launch of a Community of Practice (CoP) and invites stakeholders to provide input on its structure and objectives. Participants are encouraged to review and share feedback to help shape the CoP’s goals, membership, and operational guidelines.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This policy invites individuals or organizations to express interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP). It outlines how to submit an expression of interest and the criteria that will guide the selection process.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document explains how a Community of Practice uses an iterative drafting process to create and refine policy documents, showing each stage from initial draft to final version. It highlights the importance of continuous feedback, collaboration, and revision to improve clarity, relevance, and alignment with community goals.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document presents a graphic timeline that tracks the drafting process for a Code of Practice. It shows the key stages and milestones from the initial proposal through to the final approval of the policy.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This early draft of a code of practice for AI outlines the main principles and responsibilities that developers and users should follow. It includes guidelines on ethical design, transparency, safety, and accountability to promote trustworthy AI deployment.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document outlines the updated guidelines for ethical and responsible AI usage, detailing standards for transparency, fairness, and accountability. It serves as a framework for organizations to implement best practices and comply with emerging regulatory expectations.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document outlines a third draft of a Code of Practice, offering updated guidelines on how AI systems should be developed, deployed, and monitored to ensure safety, fairness, and transparency. It serves as a framework for organizations to follow responsible AI practices, detailing responsibilities, risk assessment processes, and accountability measures.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposed framework that outlines shared commitments to responsible AI development and deployment. It aims to bring stakeholders together to establish principles, standards, and oversight mechanisms that promote safety, transparency, and societal benefit.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a high‑level agreement that brings together governments, industry, and civil society to set shared principles for responsible AI. It outlines how to develop, regulate, and monitor AI systems so they are safe, transparent, and aligned with human values.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This policy lists the types of AI use that are not allowed. It tells developers and users which practices they must avoid when creating or deploying artificial intelligence.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: The document explains what counts as an AI system by outlining its key attributes and providing examples to help stakeholders identify such systems. It also details the responsibilities for documenting, monitoring, and ensuring compliance with the definition throughout the system’s lifecycle.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: The document outlines how effective communication can support the growth of start‑ups and spur broader innovation. It provides guidelines and best practices for engaging stakeholders, promoting policies, and showcasing success stories to create a more vibrant entrepreneurial ecosystem.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups aims to support early-stage technology companies by providing access to high-performance computing resources across Europe. It offers funding, mentorship, and infrastructure to help start-ups innovate and scale their AI and computational solutions.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The document describes a webinar focused on risk management for AI projects. It provides practical guidance on identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential risks to ensure safe and responsible AI deployment.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The policy gives clear instructions on how to manage risks when hosting AI‑focused webinars, from planning and content review to live moderation and post‑session follow‑up. It lays out steps for spotting potential hazards, judging their severity, and applying safeguards to keep participants and the platform safe.
